item.title: Nationwide ground stop over: Guam, CNMI flights were not affected
item.description: UPDATE: The Federal Aviation Administration announced the groundstop was lifted and domestic air travel was able to resume. Earlier Saturday, airport officials on Guam and in the CNMI said the nationwide grounding of domestic air traffic did not affect local airports here.
item.content:encoded:
UPDATE: The Federal Aviation Administration announced the groundstop was lifted and domestic air travel was able to resume.

Earlier Saturday, airport officials on Guam and in the CNMI said the nationwide grounding of domestic air traffic did not affect local airports here.

An announcement from the Guam International Airport Saturday said officials are “closely monitoring the situation. No Guam flights are affected as of yet, and operations remain normal.”

Travelers were advised to keep in touch with their air carriers through official mobile apps to get the latest flight information.

The airport said the situation is still developing, and “GIAA will continue to closely monitor it and share information as circumstances change.”

The Commonwealth Ports Authority said inter-island flights between Saipan, Tinian and Rota were operating normally.

While Saturday morning’s Guam flight arrived and departed from Saipan, the agency said other flights outside of the CNMI may still be delayed or canceled.

Star Marianas Air posted a social media status update Saturday saying the company’s flights were not affected by the FAA nationwide stop.

Update from The White House https://t.co/pNjkz3znSB

Early Saturday, Guam time, NPR reported that the Federal Aviation Administration issued a nationwide ground stop for all U.S. airports following a "communication issue impacting all Air Route Traffic Control Centers," according to Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy.

The FAA said the ground stop was linked to a "temporary telecommunications outage."

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin told reporters at the White House there was no indication that the problem stemmed from a threat to the United States, NPR reported.

item.content:encoded:
The Department of Public Health and Social Services is reminding families who received 2026 Summer Electronic Benefit Transfer benefits to use any remaining funds by Nov. 16.

The federally funded program helps eligible families purchase food for school-aged children during the summer months. Under federal requirements, any unused benefits will be returned to the funding source after the expiration date.

Families are encouraged to check their card balances and use their remaining benefits before Nov. 16. However, those who received their child’s card later and were given a different expiration date should follow the date provided.

Families who have not picked up their child’s Summer EBT card or need a replacement may visit the Bureau of Economic Security office on the second floor of the RanCare Building in Tamuning from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.Monday through Friday.

For assistance, families may contact the Summer EBT Call Center at (671)735-7325 or (671)735-7310, or email kidssebtguam@dphss.guam.gov .

Public Health administers the Summer EBT Program locally in partnership with the Guam Department of Education.

item.title: Hybrid Land Use Commission approves school in Tumon, extension for Tamuning subdivision
item.description: The Guam Hybrid Land Use Commission on Thursday approved using a vacant mall in Tumon as a school and granted a one-year extension for the construction of a subdivision in Tamuning. The zone variance allows the unused Tumon Bay Mall, owned by Grandview Development, to be converted to a facility that will house 40 classrooms and up to 1,080 students from iLearn Academy, a charter school.
item.content:encoded:
The Guam Hybrid Land Use Commission on Thursday approved using a vacant mall in Tumon as a school and granted a one-year extension for the construction of a subdivision in Tamuning.

The zone variance allows the unused Tumon Bay Mall, owned by Grandview Development, to be converted to a facility that will house 40 classrooms and up to 1,080 students from iLearn Academy, a charter school.

Architect Michael Blas Makio, managing principal at Taniguchi Ruth Makio Architects, said the project would be good for Tumon and good for education.

“Even driving here, we started the really sad exercise of counting the vacant buildings that we're seeing around the island, and that's a really scary growing number, right? So we’ve got to find these viable uses that we can bring into the space,” Makio said.

The vacant mall is located next to Garden Villa Hotel and across from Crowne Plaza Resort.

The Commission also granted a one-year extension for the construction of Oka Villas subdivision, located near Oka Pay-Less and Rosie’s Apartments in Tamuning.

The land has been cleared and utilities are being installed.

The subdivision will have 36 single-family residential lots, a playground and a percolation basin.
